column2: The Dark Gods Call

A rider in blackened mail comes to my hall with a message from [From.GetTitledName]. [From.GetSheHeCap] has claimed the right to call a Black Crusade and asks every warband of the faith to gather under [From.GetHerHis] banner.

The horde will fall upon [crusade_title.GetBaseName], held by [crusade_character.GetCrusadeReligionDescription] [crusade_character.GetTitledName]. It is time they learned what it costs to defy the gods.

The target is not yet set in iron. A strong warlord who marches with the horde could turn it toward a prize of more use to us.
I will think on it.
The Black Crusade gathers its strength.
My warriors are ready! To [crusade_title.GetBaseName]!
May the gods watch my fellow [Root.Religion.GetGroupName] in their slaughter.
Black Crusade for [crusade_title.GetBaseName]

The ground shakes under hoof and boot as the hosts of Chaos march south on the Black Crusade for [crusade_title.GetBaseName]. [Root.GetCrusadeLaunchFirstPart]

[Root.GetCrusadeLaunchSecondPart]

[From.Religion.GetHighGodName] will reward every warrior who wades into the slaughter.
For the Dark Gods!
The Black Crusade for [crusade_title.GetName] begins.
The northern hordes are upon us!
The Horde Turns Back

The call went out to every corner of the North, and it was not needed. Our target had worshipped the gods in secret all along, and with the horde at the border chose to declare it rather than burn.\n\nThe warlord must find other prey.
The gods are not amused.
The Black Crusade has been called off.
[Root.GetTitledName]\nYou have not yet taken up the banner. You owe me a debt, and I am calling it in. Gather your warriors and join the horde.\n[From.GetTitledName]
Then I will march.

[pleased_courtier.GetFirstName] stops me on my way out of the hall to tell me how glad [pleased_courtier.GetSheHe] was to hear I have pledged my warriors to the Black Crusade, and wishes me good slaughter.
Your words are welcome.
A letter from [pleased_participant.GetTitledName] praises my choice to march with the horde. Perhaps we should stand shoulder to shoulder when the killing starts.
A worthy sentiment.
Let us kill side by side!

A letter comes from the despicable [pleased_participant.GetTitledName]. Since we both march on [crusade_title.GetName], [pleased_participant.GetSheHe] proposes that we bury our feud until the war is done.
The gods favour the united. For now.
I would sooner put an axe in your back.

I cannot hide my hunger for the coming war. When I think of [crusade_title.GetName] burning I feel the gods closer than ever before. I never thought myself a zealot of the [Root.Religion.GetGroupName], but perhaps the gods are changing me.
Blood for the gods!

Before I leave for the war I spend a day by the water with the old thing that lives in it. It has many fine ideas about the coming battles for [crusade_title.GetName]. I am blessed to have such a friend.
Before I leave I walk out into the woods to sit with the beasts. I end up in a long talk with... well, I am not sure what it was, but it had a great deal of sense to share!
I will do my utmost!
An eye for your wisdom, you say?
We will meet again!

[displeased_courtier.GetFirstName] tells me at length exactly how ashamed [displeased_courtier.GetSheHe] is that I have broken my pledge to the horde. When the tirade is over [displeased_courtier.GetSheHe] finally leaves me in peace.
How dare [displeased_courtier.GetSheHe]?!
Perhaps it was the wrong choice.
A letter from [displeased_participant.GetTitledName]: [displeased_participant.GetSheHe] has heard I broke my pledge to the Black Crusade and no longer trusts my word.
That is none of [displeased_participant.GetHerHis] business.
A messenger brings a letter from [displeased_participant.GetTitledName], calling me a coward and an oath-breaker who has betrayed every [Root.Religion.GetGroupName] warrior in the horde.
Then let us be enemies!
Oath-Breaker

Riders go to every war camp in the North: [From.GetTitledName] has cast out the faithless [unpledging_actor.GetTitledName], who swore to march on [crusade_title.GetName] and then turned [unpledging_actor.GetHerHis] back on the horde.\n\nThe gods do not forgive the coward. [unpledging_actor.GetSheHeCap] is to be given no shelter and no mercy, and whoever takes [unpledging_actor.GetHerHis] head will be thought well of.
Faithless dog.
What did [From.GetSheHe] call me!?

[Root.GetTitledName]\nYou have still not pledged your warriors to the horde. Every warband of the [Root.Religion.GetGroupName] is wanted for the war on [crusade_title.GetName]. Join us, or send gold if you are too weak to fight.\n[From.GetTitledName]
My warriors will march.
I will send gold instead.
I need time to decide.
Neither marching nor paying may have dire consequences.
The New [new_crusader_king.GetKingQueen]

The long war for [new_crusader_king.PrimaryTitle.GetName] is over, and the land is the gods' at last. [new_crusader_king.GetDynName] has taken its throne as the beneficiary of [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName], [new_crusader_king.GetKingQueen] of a realm carved from the enemy's flesh. Holding it on the edge of the Old World will be bloody work, but all agree [new_crusader_king.GetTitledFirstName] has the strength for it.\n\nThe warlord commands the rest of the faithful to stand by this new realm, and not to let it fall back to the weak.
May [new_crusader_king.GetSheHe] hold it.
If only it had been me...
[Root.GetTitledName]\nI have not forgotten our quarrel, but you have come back to the horde when it matters. The curse on your name is lifted.\n[From.GetTitledName]
The gods are merciful. This once.
The [beneficiary_check_crusader_beneficiary.GetLordLady] of [beneficiary_check_crusader_beneficiary.PrimaryTitle.GetName]

The war was hard won, but the burning is over and the lands I fought for went to [beneficiary_check_crusader_beneficiary.GetDynName]. Holding a fief in the conquered realm will be no easy life, and I wish [beneficiary_check_crusader_beneficiary.GetHerHim] good fortune.\n\nAs my warband rides out of [beneficiary_check_crusader_beneficiary.PrimaryTitle.GetName] I look back once. I wonder what my life would have been had I stayed in [beneficiary_check_crusader_beneficiary.GetDynName]'s place.
No. [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName] is my home.
Perhaps in another life.

Greetings, [Root.GetTitledName]

I have heard that the servants of the Dark Gods have called a Black Crusade against your lands. As a fellow [From.Religion.GetName], I will stand at your side when the hordes come.
[From.GetTitledName]
I thank you, [From.GetTitledFirstName].
How much gold should I give to the Black Crusade's war chest?
A small offering. The gods will remember it.
I know just how much.
A gift worthy of my name!
I cannot spare anything.
If the Black Crusade is won, who should rule the conquered lands? I could leave it to the warlord, give the land to my beneficiary, or keep it for myself.
The warlord will decide.
If the Black Crusade is won, the warlord grants the lands to the §YChosen Lord§!. If there is none, they go to the §YBeneficiary§! of the lord who did most in the war.
My beneficiary will take them.
If the Black Crusade is won and I did most in the war, the lands go to my §YBeneficiary§!.
Why would I give MY conquest away?
If the Black Crusade is won and I did most in the war, I take the lands myself.
I will keep to my choice.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! is dead. I must find another.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! has gained land and can no longer be my beneficiary.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! is now heir to a landed title and can no longer be my beneficiary.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! has become a mercenary and can no longer be my beneficiary.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! has joined a holy order and can no longer be my beneficiary.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! is too young to be my beneficiary.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! is too sick to be my beneficiary.
My beneficiary §Y[old_crusade_beneficiary.GetDynName]§! has become a [old_crusade_beneficiary.GetAscetic] and can no longer be my beneficiary.

[Root.GetTitledName]\nKnow that I no longer favour [old_crusade_recipient.GetDynName] for the lands of [current_crusade_target_title.GetName]. When they fall they will go to [new_crusade_recipient.GetDynName].\n[From.GetTitledName]

[Root.GetTitledName]\n[old_crusade_recipient.GetDynName] is dead and will never rule [current_crusade_target_title.GetName]. When the lands fall they will go to [new_crusade_recipient.GetDynName].\n[From.GetTitledName]

[Root.GetTitledName]\n[old_crusade_recipient.GetDynName] is dead and will never rule [current_crusade_target_title.GetName]. The throne will go to [old_crusade_recipient.GetHerHis] heir [new_crusade_recipient.GetDynName] instead.\n[From.GetTitledName]
[Root.GetTitledName]\n[old_crusade_recipient.GetDynName] is dead. When [current_crusade_target_title.GetName] falls, its lands will be yours.\n[From.GetTitledName]
[Root.GetTitledName]\nI have chosen you. When [current_crusade_target_title.GetName] falls, its lands will be yours.\n[From.GetTitledName]
So be it.
The gods smile on me.

[Root.GetTitledName]\nI no longer favour [old_crusade_recipient.GetDynName] for the lands of [current_crusade_target_title.GetName]. I name nobody in [old_crusade_recipient.GetHerHis] place: let the strongest of you take them.\n[From.GetTitledName]

[Root.GetTitledName]\n[old_crusade_recipient.GetDynName] is dead and will never rule [current_crusade_target_title.GetName]. I name nobody in [old_crusade_recipient.GetHerHis] place: let the strongest of you take the lands.\n[From.GetTitledName]
I know who should have them.
Every pledged lord who left the choice to the warlord will now give the lands to their own §YBeneficiary§! instead.
[Root.GetTitledFirstName]\nThe horde marches and you are not in it. The gods see the weak, and so do I.\n[From.GetTitledFirstName]
I rule my own lands, not you.

[Root.GetTitledFirstName]\nYou swore to march with the horde, and neither you nor your warriors have shed a drop of enemy blood. Lie to me again and the gods will hear of it. I expect your warband in the field.\n[From.GetTitledName]
I suppose I should go...
[Root.GetTitledFirstName]\nYou had your warning and ignored it. A lord who swears to the gods and does not fight is no servant of theirs. From this day you are cast out.\n[From.GetTitledName]
[From.GetSheHeCap] does not sound pleased...
The Black Crusade Triumphs

[From.Religion.GetHighGodName] has given [new_crusade_most_participating_member.GetTitledName] victory in the Black Crusade for [new_crusade_title.GetBaseName]. [new_crusade_target_char.GetTitledName] was beaten at every turn and has had to give up [new_crusade_target_char.GetHerHis] lands in [new_crusade_title.GetBaseName].

[Root.GetCrusadeSelfishOrNot]

With [new_crusade_target_char.GetTitledName] driven from [new_crusade_target_char.GetHerHis] old lands, more war is certain to follow.
Praise [From.Religion.GetHighGodName]!
Gods preserve us.
Once it was a land of the gods, and warlords from all across the North have gathered to take it back.
Once it was a land of the gods, and warlords from all across the North gather to fight for it once more.
It has long lain on the edge of our lands, and [From.GetTitledName] has decided it is time to show the people of [crusade_title.GetName] the true might of Chaos.
It has long lain on the edge of our lands, and [From.GetTitledName] has decided it is time to show the people of [crusade_title.GetName] the true might of Chaos once again.
It has never been a Chaos realm, but [From.GetTitledName] has decided it is time to show the people of [crusade_title.GetName] the true might of Chaos.
It has never been a Chaos realm, but [From.GetTitledName] has decided it is time to show the people of [crusade_title.GetName] the true might of Chaos once again.
Decide what happens if the Black Crusade is won and we did most to win it. Should we leave the lands to the warlord's chosen lord, give them to our beneficiary, or take them ourselves?

I will leave the conquered lands to the warlord's chosen lord.
§Y * The gods see this as the proper way.
 * The warlord will approve.
 * I receive a larger share of the war chest.§!

I will give the conquered lands to my beneficiary.
§Y * The gods neither approve nor disapprove.
 * The warlord will neither approve nor disapprove.
 * Needs a beneficiary, or it counts as taking the lands for myself.§!

I will take the conquered lands myself if I did most to win them.
§Y * A greedy choice.
 * The warlord will disapprove.
 * I receive no share of the war chest.§!
You cannot break the pledge: the warlord called in your debt.
